full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff's case in brief is that the suit premises as described in the schedule to the plaint formerly belonged to Abbas Ali who has been made opposite party No. 2 in the present proceeding Abbas Ali acquired the premises in the suit from Bhupendra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, a Zamindar of Mathana Bara Taraf Estate and the land has been correctly recorded in the name of said Abbas  Ali in the recent Khatian, Abbas Ali constructed a house upon the disputed land and inducted the petitioner as a monthly tenant at a rent of Rs. 16/- per month according to Bengali Calendar. The petitioner paid rent unto Aswin 1372 B. S. to Abbas Ali on proper receipts but thereafter he defaulted in making payment of rent whereupon House Rent Control Case No. 30/55-56 was brought by Abbas Ali and the same ended in a compromise. Abbas Ali having been in need of money subsequently sold the disputed property to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 24-7-1967. After the purchase the plaintiff demanded rent from the petitioner who with an evil design approached the Enemy Property Authority and on misrepresentation of facts succeeded in taking settlement of the disputed premises from the Asset Custodian Enemy Property. However, on the plaintiff's representation the property was ultimately released, Grounds for ejectment are habitual default of the petitioner in regard to payment of rent as well as bonafide requirement of the suit premises for the personal use and occupation of the plaintiff. The tenancy in question has been terminated by service of notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act with effect from the 1st Baishakh, 1377 B. S.
